A proposal to explore with founding advisory firms.

The idea.

A client says, “I want to invest in this.” Your firm gets the whole picture.

What they own personally and through companies. Where the money could come from. What needs selling. Their available limits, the tax now and later, and what they want the investment to do.

They can test a plan themselves. You review the recommendation, call them with the context in front of you, and record what you agreed. Once they sign the approved version, connected systems could carry out the authorised steps.

AI would handle document classification, proposed data extraction and follow-up questions. Your professionals keep responsibility for advice, tax work and approvals.

The adviser’s desk.

Every client’s portfolio, requests, documents and filing questions in one place. Their number beside the plan. Previous conversations and notes on the right.

CLIENT REQUEST

Alex wants to invest £200,000.

Compare ownership and funding. Review tax assumptions. Ask about the preference shares.

The aim is to help a small firm serve more clients while keeping the relationship personal. The demo shows the workflow; capacity savings still need validating with a real firm.

What would it do?

01

Read the paperwork.

Documents and emails become proposed investment records, dates and questions. Grants, employee shares, contracts, statements and travel evidence stay attached.

02

Compare the plan.

Personal, company or split ownership. Growth, distributions, reinvestment, disposal and extraction. Show the source accounts, quantities and projected holdings changes.

03

Approve the instructions.

Professional review, client signature and a versioned execution plan. Sell, settle, reserve tax, transfer and invest in order. A failure stops later steps.

04

Finish the filing.

Checklists grouped by submission date and person or company. Known information is pre-filled. Clients answer what’s missing and confirm the final numbers.

Follow the journey.

Start with the customer: connect accounts, check limits, propose an investment, approve the reviewed plan and finish the filing. Then follow the firm: verify records, review the request, call the client and oversee the authorised steps.

Who would buy it?

The firm.

A regulated wealth advisory business with tax accountancy in-house, complex clients and an administrative bottleneck. The firm onboards its own clients and reviews advice before it reaches them.

The client.

A founder after an exit, business owner or executive who wants to stay hands-on. They have investments across personal accounts, companies, pensions and employee shares, and want professionals checking the decisions.

Initial customer hypothesis

£5m–25m investable portfolios, excluding the primary home. A proposed £2m entry threshold. These are discovery assumptions, not evidence of demand.

Clients get a simple view. Their adviser gets the detail and controls. Home equity counts towards wealth but is never proposed as investment funding.

The business case.

Proposed platform fee: £10,000 per client office, per year.

Shareholder accounts included. Advice, accounting, legal work and filing fees would be agreed separately. This is a pricing hypothesis, not a current service offer. The platform fee alone is 0.5% of a £2m portfolio or 0.2% of a £5m portfolio, before professional fees.

Adoption scenarioClient officesAnnual platform revenue

These are arithmetic adoption scenarios across the proposed UK/Australia market, not a measured TAM, forecast, customer count or valuation. A credible TAM needs the number of qualifying households, suitable firms and willingness to pay.

The FCA’s 2026 UK wealth report covers 500 investment-management firms and over 5.5m retail clients; typical advised portfolios are around £650k, below the proposed entry threshold. Those clients cannot all be counted as this product’s market. Australian qualifying demand remains to be measured. FCA source ↗

Built around your firm.

The proposed platform works alongside existing accounting and tax systems. Xero could handle bookkeeping and expenses; ron would add the investment, planning, documents and approvals layer.

The United Kingdom demo covers UK personal and company investing, ISA/EIS conditions, dividend and gains treatment, pensions and HMRC/Companies House obligations. See the source-dated rule register and known changes →

Advice remains with the authorised firm. Tax work remains with its registered professionals. Legal work goes to appointed lawyers. For United Kingdom, eligibility would require appropriate FCA permissions and qualified tax accountancy, AML supervision and professional registrations.
